It sounds like the audiologist only set up a general program for you, which includes all of the sound processing necessary for speech. But the gotcha is all that sound processing totally wrecks music because music is pure tones and speech obviously is  different. So the hearing aids interpret pure tones as distortion or feedback and try to eliminate it. So that's why you get those strange artifacts  you noticed swishing noises and distortion.  The answer is oticon intents have four programmable choices. Obviously the first choice is your general program. Then you can choose from speech in noise, lecture,  calm setting and the one that you'd be interested in hearing would be the music program which eliminates all of the processing needed for speech. But as I said, in my previous post the music program that oticon uses has some definite limitations. So you'd have to find a audiologist that

If they are, know that it’s a million times louder in our ears, is very uncomfortable, & drowns everything out with a screeching WHEEeEEEE , basically rendering them useless.  If they’re obviously not comfortable, please don’t force kiddo to wear them.  Paediatric hearing aids are even louder than adults’ ones, because they want to pump in all the sound under the guise of,  “speech, & sound everything access…” which, I can honestly tell you as someone with a profound loss, is absolutely overwhelming, exhausting, & even distressing after a while. >I'm curious, how does one do the DIY approach from home--aren't there certain things that can only be done through the audiologist's interface (Oticon Genie, or some such named program), which is unavailable to the layperson/user?

What's needed is a windows PC (or mac w/windows emulator running on an intel processor). You need the programming interface which connects the HAs to the programming software over bluetooth it's a Noahlink wireless which is available on amazon or ebay. Finally, a copy of the programming software for oticon which is Genie 2.

There is a learning curve, but there are ample on-line courses available at Audiology Online, as well as Oticon's website.

The best resource is hearingtracker forum, where a lot of us DIYers hang out, and there is a hidden section for self programming with access to Genie 2. hearingaid talk is another one.
